Serana: Oh darling, if I wanted Vekel, you'd be picking your entrails off these lovely stone floors right now. But don't worry - my tastes run far more... epicurean than your sad little barkeep. MJR's got more adventure in his little finger than your whole Guild's stolen silverware collection.

Tonilia: That mouth's gonna get you drained one day, bloodsucker. We don't take kindly to your kind down here, especially not ones parading around in glorified bandages. That's Delvin's little side project - some old amulet he's obsessed with.

Delvin wouldn't know true antiquities if they bit him in the ass. Tonilia: Says the walking corpse who probably fucked the original owner. Serana: At least I have standards, darling.

Tonilia: At least our stains come from honest theft, not sucking peasants dry behind the stables. Though I suppose old blood's harder to scrub out than stolen gold. Serana: ... I could buy out the entire Thieves Guild. Twice. Tonilia: That bed's seen more action than a skooma den on Saturnsday. Bet you'd know all about that, wouldn't you, vamp? Those stone walls hold more secrets than your little undead thighs. Serana: Oh, I guarantee my secrets are far more interesting than whatever sad little trysts happened under that scratchy blanket. Though if MJR wants to test the mattress with me, I could show you what five centuries of experience looks like.

Serana: Sweetheart, when you've lived as long as I have, you learn a fainting victim is just another opportunity. And trust me, nothing makes the blood pump like a little danger... Gods, even your shadows dress better than you lot.

MJR: I'll have to think about it.; Galathil: Indeed. It is no small thing to submit yourself to the flesh sculptor's knife.)

Tonilia: That one seemed uncertain about your services, Galathil. Can't say I blame him—there's something unnerving about letting someone carve into your face. Galathil: Most walk away thinking it over. Few return. But those who do understand that beauty is a weapon sharper than any dagger I've seen you carry. Tonilia: Sharp enough to cut through a mark's coin purse, I suppose. Still, at this hour, most of the folks stumbling in here aren't looking for a new nose—they're looking for a drink to forget their troubles. Galathil: Trouble and transformation often go hand in hand. A new face can be a new life, after all.

Tonilia: That view... reminds me of the passage out to the old Solitude Lighthouse. I always wondered what it'd be like to carve a new life out of stone and sea. Galathil: The Rock may be indifferent to our desires, but a face can be coaxed into anything you wish.

(Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Vex, Dirge, Vekel the Man, Delvin Mallory, Serana) (MJR: Brynjolf sent me.; Tonilia: So, you're the new recruit, huh? Well, looks like you and I are going to have to get very well acquainted. MJR: Why is that?; Tonilia: I'm the fence down here. You come by anything you don't exactly own and I'll pay you some coin for it. Minus a little slice for the Guild, of course. I can also provide a few supplies useful to our trade now and again, for a small fee. MJR: Is there anything you don't charge for?; Tonilia: Sure, how about I get Dirge to knock you over your head and dump you into the cistern? Look, I've been in this business a long time and I've seen all types. You can play it tough, or you can play it smart... whatever. At the end of the day, you'll find that all we care about down here is how much gold you can make us. MJR: Understood.; Tonilia: Good. Then there isn't much more to say. Here's your armor, just make sure you put it to good use. MJR: ...; Tonilia: Well, looks like you're fitting in well down here. I'm supposed to allow you to trade in one of your pieces of Guild armor, so what will it be? MJR: Anything different about it?; Tonilia: Of course... otherwise it wouldn't be much of a reward, now would it? Your new piece will enhance your skill beyond that of the original. Trust me. MJR: I'll trade in my boots.; Tonilia: Are you sure? Once I exchange it for you, I'm not taking it back... unless you want to sell it at a discount of course. MJR: Yes, I'm sure.; Tonilia: Okay, there you go.)

Daegon: So this is where the Guild does all its shady business. Smells like wet dog and cheap mead. I like it. Lydia: I still cannot believe we are associating with thieves and cutthroats. In Whiterun, we would have these lot thrown into the Dragonsreach dungeons. Tonilia: And yet here you are, drinking my mead and standing under my lanterns. Funny how necessity changes a Nord's principles, isn't it?

Delvin Mallory: Two in the morning and the place is still buzzing like a hive of anxious bees. Mercer's betrayal has everyone on edge. Vekel the Man: Aye, and my mead sales have doubled. Misery loves company, and cheap drink. Tonilia: Vekel, you'd sell your own mother's tears if you could bottle them. But Delvin's right. That vault being empty changes everything for us. Delvin Mallory: Empty isn't quite the word I'd use. Cleaned out like a Nord's plate after a feast. Gallus spent years building those plans, and Mercer just... walked off with them. Vekel the Man: Walked off with a key that was supposed to be impossible to copy. Brynjolf's been pacing for hours trying to figure it out. Tonilia: I've seen Mercer charm his way through plenty of locked doors. That man had more tricks than a mages' college dropout. But this... this is different. He planned this for a long time. Delvin Mallory: The question is whether he planned it alone. Someone had to help him get into that vault without the rest of us knowing.

Vekel the Man: Late night crowd tonight. Can't say I mind the extra coin, but there's a tension in the air thicker than the smoke. Tonilia: Mercer's shadow still hangs over this place. Empty vault or not, we're all waiting for the other shoe to drop. Dirge: Let him come. I've got my axe ready for whatever walks through that door. Vekel the Man: Easy there, Dirge. We need answers more than blood. Though I won't stop you if he tries anything stupid. Tonilia: The lockbox Gallus used to keep his personal notes is still missing. That's what bothers me most. Mercer knew exactly what he was after. Dirge: Gallus trusted him. We all did.
